hints: Find the coefficient $p$ of the $x$ term in $\left(4x + \frac{10}{x}\right)^3$.
Find the coefficient $q$ of the $x^{-1}$ term in $\left(2x + \frac{k}{x^2}\right)^5$.
walkthrough:
Find the term in $x$ from the expansion of $\left(4x + \frac{10}{x}\right)^3$:
$$T = \binom{3}{1} (4x)^2 \left(\frac{10}{x}\right)^1 = 3 \times 16x^2 \times \frac{10}{x} = 480x \implies p = 480$$

Find the term in $x^{-1}$ from the expansion of $\left(2x + \frac{k}{x^2}\right)^5$:
$$\text{General term: } \binom{5}{r} (2x)^{5-r} \left(\frac{k}{x^2}\right)^r = \binom{5}{r} 2^{5-r} k^r x^{5 - 3r}$$
$$\text{For } x^{-1}:\quad 5 - 3r = -1 \implies 3r = 6 \implies r = 2$$
$$T = \binom{5}{2} (2x)^3 \left(\frac{k}{x^2}\right)^2 = 10 \times 8x^3 \times \frac{k^2}{x^4} = 80k^2 x^{-1} \implies q = 80k^2$$

Use the relation $p = 6q$ to solve for $k$:
$$480 = 6(80k^2) = 480k^2 \implies k^2 = 1 \implies k = \pm 1$$
